trust_decision.summary: Whether a user may learn that an object (unit, comment, check, change, announcement) in a private/blocked project exists is decided by the queryset passed to get_object_or_404 in each view; the views look up globally by pk and only afterwards run has_perm (403) or check_access_component (404), so existing-but-hidden objects answer differently from missing ones. The project-access filter itself is gated by User.needs_project_filter, which wrongly short-circuits for 'all projects' users who have a per-project block.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'globally scoped object lookups'; a grep for get_object_or_404(Model, pk=...) in trans/views lands on show_change/comment/js views first.

fix_sites.entry_point: User.needs_project_filter, consumed by every filter_access (Unit, Check, Screenshot, Suggestion, Component, Translation, Change)
fix_sites.module_kind: auth model / permission cache (lower-level, other package)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: weblate/auth/models.py:976-984 (needs_project_filter returns False for SELECTION_ALL users even when a UserBlock exists, so every QuerySet.filter_access skips the project filter, e.g. weblate/trans/models/unit.py:424, weblate/checks/models.py:66)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: needs_project_filter is a performance shortcut in the auth package ('all projects' users can see every project), and the existing filter_access helpers are presumed correct, so a solver wrapping lookups in filter_access believes the job is done; the blocked-user-with-all-projects combination looks like an exotic neighbouring feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Global announcements (no project/category/component) must remain lookup-able so a non-privileged user still gets 403 rather than 404; show_change must still return 200 for an accessible change when ?other= contains hidden or non-integer pks (ignore, don't fail); superusers/'all projects' users without blocks must still reach private objects with no extra queries.

user shape: plain user vs SELECTION_ALL user with per-project UserBlock vs restricted component
